newsitem.title: ITALY: Giribaldi votes against Cofide result.
newsitem.headline: Giribaldi votes against Cofide result.

text.p: A representative of Italian financier Luigi Giribaldi, after earlier Tuesday voting against approval of Carlo De Benedetti's CIR industrial holding group's 1996 results, also voted against the accounts of De Benedetti's Cofide financial holding.
The Monaco-based Giribaldi, who holds 20.05 percent of Cofide and 15.27 percent of CIR, said he believed aspects of both group's dealings lacked transparency.

A statement issued on Giribaldi's behalf after his representative voted against both groups' 1996 results at annual general meetings Tuesday said he wanted to find out more about how the companies had been run in recent years.
The results of both holdings have already been published.
During the shareholders' meetings, Giribaldi's representative Ezio Gallo asked whether the groups had possessed any funds which did not show up in their balance sheets.
Gallo also asked what relations CIR and Cofide had had with jailed financier Florio Fiorini and his now defunct Swiss holding company Sasea, which collapsed in 1992 under a crushing debt burden.
Earlier, CIR Managing Director Rodolfo De Benedetti told shareholders that "Fiorini never acted as a front-man or trustee of our company." He gave the same reply at the Cofide meeting.
De Benedetti later told reporters he was surprised by Giribaldi's decision to vote against the accounts.
"Nothing has been asked of us, we have had no request (from Giribaldi) to join the board. No proposals have been made to us to which we have replied no," said De Benedetti.
